panels.title: What these numbers are, and what they are not

options.content: Measured on the **node**, from `/proc/diskstats` (iSCSI, NVMe) and `/proc/self/mountstats` (NFS, SMB) — the TrueNAS appliance publishes no per-dataset or per-zvol series, so there is nothing array-side to poll. Two consequences: **only mounted volumes appear** (an attached-but-unmounted volume reports nothing), and **a volume's series moves between node exporters when its pod reschedules**, which reads as a counter reset on a new series. Always `sum(rate(...))`, never `rate(sum(...))`. SMB reports bytes only — the cifs client counts no operations and no latency. `pvc` is empty unless the PersistentVolume carries the claim name; join on `persistentvolume` with `kube_persistentvolume_claim_ref` to recover it.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, persistentvolume, pvc, pod) (rate(truenas_csi_volume_read_ops_total{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolume=~"$volume", pvc=~"$pvc"}[$range]))
sum by (namespace, persistentvolume, pvc, pod) (rate(truenas_csi_volume_write_ops_total{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolume=~"$volume", pvc=~"$pvc"}[$range]))
sum by (namespace, persistentvolume, pvc, pod) (rate(truenas_csi_volume_read_bytes_total{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolume=~"$volume", pvc=~"$pvc"}[$range]))
sum by (namespace, persistentvolume, pvc, pod) (rate(truenas_csi_volume_write_bytes_total{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolume=~"$volume", pvc=~"$pvc"}[$range]))

panels.title: Read latency (mean per operation)
panels.description: Cumulative time divided by cumulative operations over the same window — the division is done here, in PromQL, because the exporter publishes only the raw counters. Block volumes report device service time; NFS reports RPC round-trip time. SMB reports neither and is absent.

targets.expr:
sum by (namespace, persistentvolume, pvc, pod) (rate(truenas_csi_volume_read_seconds_total{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolume=~"$volume", pvc=~"$pvc"}[$range]))
/
sum by (namespace, persistentvolume, pvc, pod) (rate(truenas_csi_volume_read_ops_total{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolume=~"$volume", pvc=~"$pvc"}[$range]))

sum by (namespace, persistentvolume, pvc, pod) (rate(truenas_csi_volume_write_seconds_total{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolume=~"$volume", pvc=~"$pvc"}[$range]))
/
sum by (namespace, persistentvolume, pvc, pod) (rate(truenas_csi_volume_write_ops_total{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolume=~"$volume", pvc=~"$pvc"}[$range]))

panels.title: Block device utilisation
panels.description: The rate of io_ticks: the fraction of wall-clock time the volume's block device had at least one request in flight. Block volumes only; a value approaching 1 means the device is never idle.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, persistentvolume, pvc, pod) (rate(truenas_csi_volume_io_busy_seconds_total{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolume=~"$volume", pvc=~"$pvc"}[$range]))

panels.title: Volumes reporting on each node
panels.description: How many volumes each node exporter currently reports. A volume moving between nodes moves its series with it; this panel is where that shows up.

panels.title: Capacity exhaustion (from the appliance, collected by the controller)
Pool free space, with a 7-day linear projection
panels.description: The projection is predict_linear over the last 6 hours. It is a straight line through recent history, not a forecast: a pool that has just started filling will be predicted to exhaust far sooner than it will.

panels.title: Datasets projected to exhaust their quota within 7 days
panels.description: predict_linear over 6 hours of used bytes, compared with the dataset's provisioned capacity. Dell's CSM ships the same panel; the difference is that these figures cost the appliance one collection a minute rather than a poll per volume.
